Job Description
The Senior Software Quality Engineer (SSQE) plays a critical role in assuring quality (adherence to requirements and user experience) by testing the company's applications. This role shares ownership over moderate to complex architecture developments, including strategy, plan, framework, and solution development.

The SSQE is responsible for creating automation frameworks from scratch, solving high complexity problems, developing Continuous Testing (CT) models, and acting as a Point of Contact (POC) for technical guidance across the product domain.

They exhibit advanced, wide-ranging experience, using in-depth professional knowledge, acumen, and concepts to develop and resolve complex models and procedures creatively and effectively.

Defines, develops, and implements quality assurance best practices and procedures: test strategies, test plans, test cases, and other quality-related assessments for their Domain.
Participates in all aspects of testing, including functional, regression, integration, and test planning.
Works collaboratively with their team during all project stages to provide in-process testing results.
Designs, writes, executes, and maintains automated and manual tests, as well as frameworks for UI tests.
Augments development teams by enhancing test coverage where needed.
Investigates, records, triages, and tracks defects, and verifies their fixes.
Participates in code releases and the code review process.
Stays up-to-date with new testing tools and test strategies.
Provides leadership, guidance, training, and mentoring to implement quality validations and initiatives for the domain.
AI Integration: Leverages generative AI coding assistants to optimize framework scripting, and implements prompt engineering methodologies to draft automated test workflows and generate scalable test datasets.

Experience: 6+ years of related professional experience.
Computer science degree or demonstrable experience.
Technical Expertise (High): UI Web Automation, UI Desktop Automation, UI Web/Mobile/Desktop Functional/Manual, STLC & QA Concepts, Test Planning and Strategizing, Management of Test Data. Proficient on OOLPs and test frameworks like: Selenium (Mandatory) and Playwright (desired).
Technical Expertise (Medium-High): CI/CD/CT (Jenkins, Git, etc.), UI Mobile Automation, AWS (S3, Lambda, EC2, CloudWatch), Agile (Scrum & Kanban), Test Management. API Automation, API Testing (Manual).
AI and Modern QA Competency (Medium-High - Mandatory): Practical application of Generative AI tools (e.g., Copilot, ChatGPT) for script generation and maintenance, test documentation, and failure logs analysis.
Problem Solving: Proven ability to understand and work on complex issues requiring in-depth evaluation of variable factors, exercising judgment in selecting methods and techniques.
Impact: Capacity to assist in designing functional plans to prevent critical delays and production bugs.
Collaboration: Networks effectively with key contacts outside their immediate area of expertise. Acts as a Technical Lead and Mentor, actively influencing development and QA peers to adopt modern quality standards, participate in incident reviews, and champion a shared-ownership culture for code quality.
Nice to have experience with accessibility and performance testing.

READY TO MAKE AN IMPACT? If you are passionate about industrial automation, solving complex technical challenges, and building something from the ground up, join our team as an Industrial Automation Engineer.
The machinery is the easy part to buy. The control system that turns it into a plant - and the standards, documentation, and data that keep it running - is what we are hiring you to own.
We are looking for an experienced Industrial Automation Engineer to take ownership of our plant’s control systems from design through commissioning and into stable production. You bring deep hands-on experience in programming and commissioning industrial control systems and are comfortable taking responsibility for the PLC, safety systems, HMI, industrial networking, and interfaces between multiple machine suppliers.

Join our international team, help build innovative solutions for scrap metal processing, and contribute to a more sustainable future.
YOUR MISSION PLC & Plant Control: Design, write, and own the PLC program using Siemens TIA Portal / S7-1200 & S7-1500, including control logic, sequencing, fault handling, and HMI
Commissioning & Production: Take the plant from design through commissioning to a stable, running line, owning the full journey through FAT/SAT and the hands-on work required to make the plant genuinely reliable
Plant Availability: Design stop and interlock behaviour to minimise unnecessary downtime — allowing unaffected parts of the plant to keep running when it is safe to do so. Plant availability is a direct business outcome here, and you will directly influence it
Machine Safety: Implement the machine-safety control concept on a fail-safe F-CPU with F-I/O, including the hardwired e-stop loop, PLC-enforced zone isolation that cannot be overridden, guard interlocks, and controlled, sequenced shutdown
Safety & Compliance: Be our in-house technical counterpart on EN ISO 13849 performance-level determination and the CE file, working with external assessors while retaining ownership of the technical approach and decisions
Machine Integration: Integrate control systems from several different machine suppliers into one coherent line, so that a single stop is genuinely a single stop across the whole plant
Supplier Management: Hold machine builders and panel builders to specification, including unlocked code, complete documentation, and standards compliance
OT / IT & Industrial IoT: Get plant data out over OPC UA / MQTT / Modbus TCP into our own systems, so stoppage reasons, energy use, and throughput become actionable data. Work closely with our Industrial IoT team, who own the edge and data side of that boundary

Deep Siemens TIA Portal / S7-1200 & S7-1500 experience, with strong skills in SCL, LAD/FBD, HMI/SCADA, industrial networking (PROFINET, PROFIBUS, Modbus TCP), drives/VFDs, and fault-finding
Strong machine safety competence, including F-CPU / Safety Integrated and EN ISO 13849, with the ability to explain and defend performance-level determinations
Comfortable reading electrical schematics and troubleshooting cabinets, hardware, signals, wiring, and control behaviour directly on the shop floor. You have brought at least one production line from commissioning into stable production; maintenance-only experience is not sufficient

Prove Partners is consolidating two Salesforce orgs and migrating a legacy system of record into Salesforce. The program runs in continuous release cycles, and every cycle changes objects, page layouts, permission sets, flows, Apex, and integrations. Each of those changes has to be proven out end to end before it reaches production users.
We are looking for a junior Salesforce administrator (remote) who wants to spend the bulk of their time in structured, repeatable quality assurance. This person will execute full end-to-end test passes in our sandboxes, over and over, across each release: building and maintaining the test scripts, running them, logging what breaks, retesting fixes, and confirming regressions have not been introduced elsewhere.
Repetition is the job, not a side effect of it. The right candidate is someone who is genuinely comfortable running the same 200-step regression pass every sprint and catching the one step that changed — and who is methodical enough to keep the documentation accurate while doing it. Engagement at a Glance
Working title Junior Salesforce Administrator / QA Tester Reports to Director of Program Management & CRM Location Offshore / nearshore, fully remote Time zone requirement Minimum 6 hours of daily overlap with 9:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. US Eastern Commitment Full-time, 40 hours per week Duration 6–12 months, with option to extend Engagement type Open — vendor staff augmentation, individual contractor, or employer-of-record Seniority Junior (1–3 years); this is a hands-on execution role, not a lead role
Time zone is a hard requirement. Testing is iterative and conversational — the tester needs to be able to ask an administrator or developer a question and get an answer inside the same working session. Candidates should be located where the standard working day overlaps with US Eastern. Key Responsibilities
End-to-end and regression testing (primary, ~60% of time)
Execute full end-to-end test passes across core business processes in the sandbox environments, following documented scripts, for every release cycle.
Run regression suites after each configuration or code change to confirm that existing functionality still behaves as expected.
Test across the full record lifecycle — record creation, field updates, stage and status transitions, automation firing, downstream record effects, and reporting output.
Retest and close out defects after fixes are deployed, and confirm the fix has not broken adjacent functionality.
Validate behavior after sandbox refreshes and deployments, including smoke testing of critical paths.
Test design and documentation (~20% of time)
Write and maintain test cases and test scripts from user stories, acceptance criteria, and process documentation.
Keep the test case library current as requirements change; retire cases that no longer apply and add coverage for new functionality.
Log defects with clear, reproducible steps, expected vs. actual results, affected records, screenshots, and severity.
Maintain test execution records so that release readiness can be assessed at a glance.
Test data and environment support (~10% of time)
Prepare and refresh test data sets, including bulk loads via Data Loader or Data Import Wizard.
Write basic SOQL queries to verify data state and confirm expected record changes.
Test across multiple user profiles and permission sets to confirm record visibility, field-level security, and sharing behave correctly for each role.
Light administrative configuration (~10% of time)
Perform straightforward declarative configuration under supervision — custom fields, page layouts, list views, validation rules, simple reports and dashboards.
Assist with user setup, permission set assignment, and access troubleshooting.
Support user acceptance testing cycles: prepare UAT scripts, walk business testers through them, and consolidate their feedback.

1–3 years of hands-on experience in a Salesforce environment as an administrator, QA tester, business analyst, or support analyst.
Working knowledge of the Salesforce platform: standard and custom objects, record types, page layouts, profiles and permission sets, validation rules, and Flow.
Demonstrated experience executing manual test cases and logging defects in a tracked system (Jira, Azure DevOps, or similar).
Ability to read a user story or acceptance criteria and translate it into concrete test steps.
Comfort with repetitive, detail-intensive work and a track record of sustained accuracy in it.
Basic SOQL and comfort with Data Loader or a comparable data tool.
Clear written and spoken English — defect reports and test notes are read by developers and business stakeholders, so writing quality matters.
Availability for the required daily overlap with US Eastern business hours.

Experience testing during a data migration or multi-org consolidation.
Exposure to integration testing between Salesforce and external systems, including basic API concepts.
Familiarity with Jira, Confluence, or comparable tracking and documentation tools.
Any experience with test automation (Selenium, Provar, Playwright) or reading Apex test results — useful, but this role is manual-first.
Background in healthcare, insurance, legal services, or another regulated environment where access control and audit trails matter.

By 15 days: has run a full end-to-end pass on at least one core process independently, using existing scripts, and is logging usable defects without rework.
By 30 days: is authoring new test cases from user stories with minimal correction, and owns the regression suite for at least one functional area.
By 60 days: is the reliable go-to for release readiness on their areas — the team trusts that if this person has signed off, the release is safe to deploy.
